In 6-dimensional [[geometry]], the '''1<sub>22</sub>''' polytope is a [[uniform polytope]], constructed from the [[E6 (mathematics)|E<sub>6</sub>]] group. It was first published in [[E. L. Elte]]'s 1912 listing of semiregular polytopes, named as V<sub>72</sub> (for its 72 vertices).<ref>Elte, 1912</ref>

Its [[Coxeter symbol]] is '''1<sub>22</sub>''', describing its bifurcating [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]], with a single ring on the end of the 1-node sequence. There are two rectifications of the 1<sub>22</sub>, constructed by positions points on the elements of 1<sub>22</sub>. The '''rectified 1<sub>22</sub>''' is constructed by points at the mid-edges of the '''1<sub>22</sub>'''. The '''birectified 1<sub>22</sub>''' is constructed by points at the triangle face centers of the '''1<sub>22</sub>'''.

These polytopes are from a family of 39 convex [[uniform 6-polytope|uniform polytopes in 6-dimensions]], made of [[uniform 5-polytope|uniform polytope]] facets and [[vertex figure]]s, defined by all permutations of rings in this [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]]: {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}}.
{{-}}

The 1<sub>22</sub> polytope contains 72 vertices, and 54 [[5-demicube|5-demicubic]] facets. It has a [[birectified 5-simplex]] [[vertex figure]]. Its 72 vertices represent the root vectors of the [[simple Lie group]] [[E6 (mathematics)|E<sub>6</sub>]].

=== Alternate names ===
* '''Pentacontatetrapeton''' (Acronym: mo) - 54-facetted polypeton (Jonathan Bowers)<ref>Klitzing, (o3o3o3o3o *c3x - [http://bendwavy.org/klitzing/incmats/mo.htm mo])</ref>

=== Construction ===
It is created by a [[Wythoff construction]] upon a set of 6 [[hyperplane]] mirrors in 6-dimensional space.

The facet information can be extracted from its [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]], {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch_01lr|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}}.

Removing the node on either of 2-length branches leaves the [[5-demicube]], 1<sub>21</sub>, {{CDD|nodea|3a|branch_01lr|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}}.

The [[vertex figure]] is determined by removing the ringed node and ringing the neighboring node. This makes the [[birectified 5-simplex]], 0<sub>22</sub>, {{CDD|node|3|node|3|node_1|3|node|3|node}}.

Seen in a [[configuration (polytope)|configuration matrix]], the element counts can be derived by mirror removal and ratios of [[Coxeter group#Properties|Coxeter group]] orders.<ref name=:0>Coxeter, Regular Polytopes, 11.8 Gosset figures in six, seven, and eight dimensions, pp. 202–203</ref>

=== Related complex polyhedron ===
[[File:Complex polyhedron 3-3-3-4-2.png|thumb|Orthographic projection in Aut(E6) Coxeter plane with 18-gonal symmetry for complex polyhedron, <sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub>{4}<sub>2</sub>. It has 72 vertices, 216 3-edges, and 54 3{3}3 faces.]]
The [[regular complex polytope|regular complex polyhedron]] <sub>3</sub>{3}<sub>3</sub>{4}<sub>2</sub>, {{CDD|3node_1|3|3node|4|node}}, in <math>\mathbb{C}^2</math> has a real representation as the ''1<sub>22</sub>'' polytope in 4-dimensional space. It has 72 vertices, 216 3-edges, and 54 3{3}3 faces. Its [[complex reflection group]] is <sub>3</sub>[3]<sub>3</sub>[4]<sub>2</sub>, order 1296. It has a half-symmetry quasiregular construction as {{CDD|3node|3|3node_1|3|3node}}, as a [[rectification (geometry)|rectification]] of the [[Hessian polyhedron]], {{CDD|3node_1|3|3node|3|3node}}.<ref> Coxeter, H. S. M., ''Regular Complex Polytopes'', (1991) second edition, Cambridge University Press, p. 30 and p. 47</ref>

=== Related polytopes and honeycomb ===
Along with the semiregular polytope, '''[[Gosset 2 21 polytope|2<sub>21</sub>]]''', it is also one of a family of 39 convex [[uniform polytope]]s in 6-dimensions, made of [[uniform polytope]] facets and [[vertex figure]]s, defined by all permutations of rings in this [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]]: {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}}.

{{1 k2 polytopes}}

==== Geometric folding ====
The '''1<sub>22</sub>''' is related to the [[24-cell]] by a geometric [[Folding (Dynkin diagram)|folding]] E6 → F4 of [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]]s, E6 corresponding to '''1<sub>22</sub>''' in 6 dimensions, F4 to the 24-cell in 4 dimensions. This can be seen in the [[Coxeter plane]] projections. The 24 vertices of the 24-cell are projected in the same two rings as seen in the 1<sub>22</sub>.

==== Tessellations ====
This polytope is the [[vertex figure]] for a [[Uniform honeycomb|uniform tessellation]] of 6-dimensional space, '''[[2 22 honeycomb|2<sub>22</sub>]]''', {{CDD|node_1|3|node|3|node|split1|nodes|3ab|nodes}}.

The '''rectified 1<sub>22</sub>''' polytope (also called '''0<sub>221</sub>''') can tessellate 6-dimensional space as the [[Voronoi cell]] of the [[E6 honeycomb|E6* honeycomb]] lattice (dual of E6 lattice).<ref>[http://home.digital.net/~pervin/publications/vermont.html The Voronoi Cells of the E6* and E7* Lattices] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160130193811/http://home.digital.net/~pervin/publications/vermont.html |date=2016-01-30 }}, Edward Pervin</ref>

=== Construction ===
Its construction is based on the [[E6 (mathematics)|E<sub>6</sub>]] group and information can be extracted from the ringed [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]] representing this polytope: {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch_10|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}}.

Removing the ring on the short branch leaves the [[birectified 5-simplex]], {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|nodea_1|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}}.

Removing the ring on either of 2-length branches leaves the [[birectified 5-orthoplex]] in its alternated form: '''t<sub>2</sub>(2<sub>11</sub>)''', {{CDD|nodea|3a|branch_10|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}}.

The [[vertex figure]] is determined by removing the ringed node and ringing the neighboring ring. This makes [[3-3 duoprism prism]], {3}×{3}×{}, {{CDD|node|3|node_1|2|node_1|2|node_1|3|node}}.

Seen in a [[Configuration (polytope)|configuration matrix]], the element counts can be derived by mirror removal and ratios of [[Coxeter group#Properties|Coxeter group]] orders.<ref name=":0" />{{r|ram}}

=== Alternate names ===
* Truncated 1<sub>22</sub> polytope (Acronym: tim)<ref>Klitzing, (o3o3x3o3o *c3x - [http://bendwavy.org/klitzing/incmats/tim.htm tim])</ref>

=== Construction ===
Its construction is based on the [[E6 (mathematics)|E<sub>6</sub>]] group and information can be extracted from the ringed [[Coxeter-Dynkin diagram]] representing this polytope: {{CDD|nodea|3a|nodea|3a|branch_11|3a|nodea|3a|nodea}}.
